d: Binance is a leading global blockchain ecosystem behind the world’s largest cryptocurrency exchange by trading volume and registered users. We are trusted by 300+ million people in 100+ countries for our industry-leading security, user fund transparency, trading engine speed, deep liquidity, and an unmatched portfolio of digital-asset products. Binance offerings range from trading and finance to education, research, payments, institutional services, and more. Our mission is to increase the freedom of money and financial access for people around the world.

We are looking for a Policy & Change Management Specialist to strengthen governance and operational effectiveness across the Compliance function. You will drive the end-to-end policy lifecycle, change management, governance reporting and risk oversight, ensuring compliance frameworks remain accurate, consistent and audit-ready across multiple jurisdictions. You will also have the opportunity to leverage AI and automation to modernize governance processes, improve efficiency and strengthen risk oversight, partnering closely with Compliance, Legal, Product and Internal Controls teams.
q: 3–5+ years of experience in compliance policy governance, change management or regulatory program management within financial services.
Working knowledge of AML/BSA, sanctions compliance and country risk requirements.
Proven experience managing policy/document governance, change management workflows, approvals, attestations and audit-ready records.
Experience supporting regulatory examinations, audits or internal control reviews, including evidence coordination and remediation tracking.
Strong capabilities in governance reporting, stakeholder coordination, documentation and managing multiple priorities across jurisdictions.
Proficiency in Confluence, document management systems, structured trackers and dashboards.
Familiarity with AI tools for research, drafting, analysis and workflow automation, with sound judgment in handling confidential information.
Experience in the cryptocurrency, digital assets or fintech industry.
Exposure to regulatory change monitoring, country risk assessments and multi-jurisdictional compliance frameworks.
Experience implementing AI-driven workflow automation or governance process improvements.
Collaborate with world-class talent in a user-centric global organization with a flat structure
Tackle challenging projects in a fast-paced and innovative enviornment with autonomy
Thrive in a results-driven workplace with opportunities for career growth and continuous learning
Remote-first, work-from-home arrangement (may vary depending on the nature of the role and team)
Binance is committed to being an equal opportunity employer. We believe that having a diverse workforce is fundamental to our success.

r: Manage the global and local compliance policy lifecycle, including document governance, version control, periodic reviews, approvals and central repository maintenance.
Drive end-to-end policy and process change management, including impact assessments, stakeholder communications, implementation tracking and adherence to agreed timelines.
Coordinate governance processes covering attestations, exceptions, deviations and remediation actions, ensuring timely approvals, follow-ups and accurate record keeping.
Monitor the Compliance Roadmap, country risk ratings and regulatory developments, supporting risk assessments, annual recalibrations and implementation updates.
Deliver governance reporting, year-end policy assessments and audit or regulatory support, ensuring accurate documentation, evidence management and timely issue resolution.
Partner with Compliance, Legal, Product, Internal Controls and senior stakeholders to address policy and process queries and strengthen governance frameworks.
Drive AI-enabled automation and workflow enhancements to improve governance efficiency, reporting accuracy and risk oversight.

d: As a Senior Data Engineer, you will build the pipelines and models the rest of DZ will run on. DZ operates across several verticals and markets: digital goods, ticketing, travel and trading, in Iraq, the UAE and KSA. Each has grown its own reporting and its own version of the numbers. As one of the first engineers in the new data team, you will own core parts of the data platform end to end, from ingestion off operational systems and third parties through to the modeled tables that finance, commercial and product use to make decisions, and the path that takes data science models from notebook to production. This role is about making data correct, fresh and trusted by default, so the answer stops depending on who pulled it.
q: 5 to 8 years building production software or data systems, with 3+ years in data engineering owning pipelines the business depended on.
Expert SQL and strong Python, solid dimensional modelling, and the judgment to choose the right model for the use case.
Hands-on experience with a cloud warehouse and modern orchestration and transformation tooling (for example dbt, Airflow or Dagster), plus working knowledge of Postgres and AWS.

Hands-on experience deploying and operating ML models in production alongside data scientists: feature pipelines, batch or real-time serving, model versioning, and monitoring (for example with MLflow, SageMaker or similar).
Experience with both batch and streaming ingestion, including change data capture, late and duplicate events, and schema evolution.
A correctness mindset: you reconcile numbers against the source, and you know a pipeline that runs green can still be wrong.
Communication that lands with technical and non-technical audiences, including the patience to get stakeholders to agree on what a metric means.
Analytics experience on e-commerce, payments, marketplace or fintech products, including multi-currency and multi-market reporting.
Experience with a feature store or MLOps platform, or with ML use cases such as fraud, risk or personalisation.
Experience on an early-stage data team, or consolidating fragmented reporting across business units.
Familiarity with TypeScript or Go, to work comfortably in the services that produce DZ's data.
r: Design, build and own production pipelines end to end, batch and streaming: ingestion from DZ's services (Postgres/Aurora, event streams) and third-party providers, with idempotent loads and backfills that are safe to rerun.
Model data for the warehouse and the semantic layer, turning agreed metric definitions into tested, documented models that give the same answer every time.

Treat data quality as part of the job, not a cleanup: tests, freshness SLAs, lineage and alerting that catch upstream breaks before a stakeholder does. You'll be an active participant in the team's on-call.
Partner with data science to take models from notebook to production: feature pipelines, training datasets, model deployment and serving, and monitoring for drift and data quality once they are live.
Work with product and engineering teams on event tracking and data contracts, so instrumentation is designed into services rather than bolted on, and schema changes stop silently breaking pipelines.
Handle sensitive data correctly by design: access control, masking and retention for PII (passport and telecom identifiers) across markets with different regulatory expectations.
Weigh cost against value in warehouse compute, storage and tooling, and make the tradeoffs visible.
Use AI-assisted development with judgment: review generated SQL and pipeline code like a peer PR, and check it against real data, not only whether it runs.
Mentor teammates and keep the platform legible through runbooks, ADRs and documented models, so you are not the only person who can support a critical pipeline.
x: Immediate, large-scale impact on a high-growth business
Work alongside top regional talent, with team members from Talabat, Careem, Etisalat, and more

d: HSBC Saudi Arabia provides investment banking services to the full spectrum of corporate and institutional clients in both the private and government sectors, including public companies; private companies and establishments; funds; government agencies; and family businesses and offices.

Lead the coordination, execution and continuous improvement of the Non-Financial Risk framework for Fund Administration across MENA, while providing dedicated NFR coverage for the Saudi Custody business and supporting all Saudi SSV NFR activities. The role is based in Saudi Arabia and combines regional product expertise with hands-on country risk and control responsibilities.

Act as a trusted 1LoD partner to business management, Risk and Control Owners, Operations and Technology, providing constructive challenge, practical guidance and decision-ready reporting. Strengthen front-to-back controls, identify emerging risks, oversee remediation and embed NFR into business-as-usual activity and change delivery, working closely with the Second and Third Lines of Defence.
q: Produce concise, decision-ready regional Fund Administration and Saudi SSV management information covering risk profiles, RCAs, control effectiveness, incidents, issues, audit actions and risk appetite performance.

Coordinate relevant governance agendas, papers, decisions and action tracking; attend country and regional forums and deputise when formally delegated. Committee membership and delegated authority are subject to approval.
r: The role is drafted as a first line business risk and control role, working closely with second line risk and compliance functions and third line Internal Audit. Business, product and control owners retain accountability for their risks and controls; specialist product leads retain their product responsibilities. This role provides regional coordination, oversight and challenge and does not replace independent second or third line assurance.
Lead a coordinated, risk-based Fund Administration NFR agenda across MENA, agreeing priorities with regional SSV NFR leadership, Fund Administration management and country stakeholders.

Develop and maintain a consolidated view of the regional product risk profile, including material exposures, control weaknesses, incidents, issues, emerging risks and risk appetite indicators; highlight country-specific differences and cross-market dependencies.

Coordinate the maintenance and trigger-based refresh of Fund Administration Risk and Control Assessments (RCAs), covering front-to-back activities across Business, Operations, Technology and outsourced or shared-service arrangements.

Provide subject-matter oversight and challenge of controls over fund accounting, NAV calculation and release, valuation and price sourcing, cash and securities reconciliations, transaction processing, corporate actions, fees and expense accruals, and investor or client reporting. Include investor servicing, distributions and regulatory reporting where within the service scope.

Assess risks arising from late or inaccurate NAVs, valuation discrepancies, reconciliation breaks, manual adjustments, data quality failures, missed service deadlines and inadequate review or approval controls; ensure escalation and remediation follow applicable policy.

Coordinate risk-based assurance, control monitoring and thematic reviews with country teams and relevant assurance functions. Promote consistent control standards and evidence quality without displacing local ownership or regulatory requirements.
Lead regional analysis of Fund Administration incidents and recurring themes. Translate lessons learned into preventive actions and share relevant findings across markets to reduce repeat events.

Embed NFR assessment into fund launches, client onboarding, migrations, product enhancements, system changes and material operating-model changes. Challenge control design, readiness, contingency arrangements and post-implementation assurance.

Coordinate oversight of outsourcing, third-party dependencies, cross-border service delivery and operational resilience relevant to Fund Administration, working with specialist Risk Stewards and accountable owners.
Act as the regional coordination point for Fund Administration NFR matters, partnering with global product NFR teams and supporting regional or global policy, governance and assurance initiatives.
Agree a regional delivery plan with clear responsibilities, dependencies and milestones; maintain regular engagement with country NFR, Product and Operations stakeholders.

Ensure regional standards are translated into locally appropriate controls. Escalate material gaps, conflicting requirements and resource constraints to the appropriate regional and country governance forums.
Coordinate regional recommendations and remediation, with implementation and sign-off remaining with the authorised country, business, Risk or Control Owner
Provide hands-on NFR oversight and challenge across Saudi Custody activities (Business), including Direct Custody and Clearing and Global Custody where offered/

Monitor custody-specific risks, including unresolved reconciliation breaks, settlement failures, inaccurate records, missed corporate action elections, inappropriate access or authorisation, and market infrastructure or service-provider dependencies.

Coordinate Custody RCAs, control assurance, risk indicators, incident review and remediation. Support changes to services, market access arrangements, systems and operating models with documented risk assessment and readiness evidence.
4. Support all Saudi SSV NFR activities

Support the Head of Saudi SSV and regional NFR leadership in executing the country SSV NFR agenda across all local products and services, including Fund Administration, Custody and other SSV activities where undertaken.

Coordinate policy interpretation and implementation, including relevant Group Risk Management Framework, NFR and FIM requirements. Work with local Compliance and specialist Risk Stewards on applicable Saudi requirements and regulatory changes.
Maintain an accurate and current country risk profile, supporting RCAs, enterprise-wide risk assessments where required, risk appetite monitoring, key risk indicators and escalation of breaches.

Coordinate timely recording, classification and escalation of incidents, losses, near misses and issues in the approved risk systems. Challenge root-cause analysis and track specific, owned and time-bound corrective and preventive actions.

Support audit, assurance and regulatory engagements, including preparation, evidence gathering, response coordination, management updates and tracking of findings and commitments through sustainable remediation.
Support the preparation and validation of SSV inputs to regulatory submissions and risk questionnaires, ensuring documented review and authorised sign-off by the accountable owners.

Coordinate NFR support for third-party risk, business continuity and operational resilience, information and cyber security, access controls and segregation of duties, fraud prevention, data risk and record retention with the relevant specialists.

Partner with Compliance, Financial Crime, Legal and other control functions on relevant business controls, including client onboarding, KYC dependencies, conflicts of interest, conduct and client outcomes.

Provide risk input to country product launches, client due diligence requests, business initiatives and material change. Support awareness, training and escalation during disruptions or heightened risk situations.
4. Embedding NFR into change (products, digital, resilience)
Ensure NFR is embedded into product development and change execution: control design, testing approach, go-live readiness and post-implementation assurance.
Partner with Product, Technology and Operations to reduce late-stage control gaps and strengthen operational resilience and change discipline.

Ensure transparent reporting of material exposures, overdue actions and repeat events. Validate closure evidence and the sustainability of remediation, and escalate disputed ratings, proposed risk acceptances or unresolved control gaps to the authorised decision-makers. No risk acceptance or exception approval authority is implied by this role.
Contribute to continuous improvement efforts to streamline risk and control processes (control rationalisation, simplification, automation).

Apply data/analytics (and where appropriate AI-enabled techniques) to improve risk identification, monitoring and reporting, ensuring suitable governance, documentation, testing evidence, and sustainable BAU controls.
